system: You are a formal-methods engineer. You translate design documents into precise PDDL planning problems that a classical planner can analyse.
prompt:
--- Design document ---
Limited-edition drop: stock reservation design (design doc)

The shop has 1 unit of a limited-edition item in stock, and 2 customers (c1, c2) try to buy
it at the same time. Each customer's checkout runs on its own server thread; the threads interleave
arbitrarily. A checkout first reserves a unit (a hold), then the customer pays to confirm the
purchase.

Holds are temporary: a hold that is not paid for expires after 1 clock tick, and the unit goes
back into stock so that another customer can buy it. Customers can be slow to pay; the payment step
may happen at any later time.

Reserving. The checkout thread reserves with a single atomic conditional update
(UPDATE stock SET count = count - 1 WHERE count > 0); if no row is updated the customer is told the
item is sold out.

Paying. The payment service confirms an order only if the customer's hold is still active; payment
for an expired hold is refused and the customer must start again.

Initially all customers are browsing and the stock count is 1.

--- Event model ---
The possible events in this system are modelled by the following STRIPS planning domain. Each action
is one event; it can happen only when its precondition holds, and its effect updates the state
(closed world: facts not stated are false).

```pddl
(define (domain inventory)
  (:requirements :strips :typing)
  (:types customer level tick)
  (:predicates
    ;; --- design facts (which of these hold depends on the design) ---
    (mode-1)
    (mode-4)
    (mode-3)
    (mode-2)
    ;; --- static counters ---
    (next-level ?lower ?higher - level)  ; stock level ?higher is one more than ?lower
    (zero-tick ?t - tick)
    (next-tick ?t ?u - tick)
    (hold-limit ?t - tick)               ; hold age at which a hold expires
    ;; --- state ---
    (stock ?q - level)                   ; current stock level
    (browsing ?c - customer)             ; customer has not started checkout
    (read-1 ?c - customer ?q - level) ; (racy) checkout of ?c read stock level ?q
    (holding ?c - customer)              ; customer holds one reserved unit
    (hold-age ?c - customer ?t - tick)
    (expired ?c - customer)              ; customer's hold expired and its unit went back to stock
    (sold ?c - customer))                ; customer's purchase is confirmed

  (:action read-1
    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p - level)
    :precondition (and (mode-1) (browsing ?c) (stock ?q) (next-level ?p ?q))
    :effect (and (not (browsing ?c)) (read-1 ?c ?q)))
  (:action write-stock
    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p ?cur - level ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (read-1 ?c ?q) (next-level ?p ?q) (stock ?cur) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (read-1 ?c ?q)) (not (stock ?cur)) (stock ?p) (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t)))
  (:action reserve-1
    :parameters (?c - customer ?q ?p - level ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (mode-4) (browsing ?c) (stock ?q) (next-level ?p ?q) (zero-tick ?t))
    :effect (and (not (browsing ?c)) (not (stock ?q)) (stock ?p) (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t)))
  (:action hold-ages
    :parameters (?c - customer ?t ?u - tick)
    :precondition (and (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t) (next-tick ?t ?u))
    :effect (and (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (hold-age ?c ?u)))
  (:action expire-hold
    :parameters (?c - customer ?t - tick ?q ?r - level)
    :precondition (and (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t) (hold-limit ?t) (stock ?q) (next-level ?q ?r))
    :effect (and (not (holding ?c)) (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (not (stock ?q)) (stock ?r) (expired ?c)))
  (:action pay
    :parameters (?c - customer ?t - tick)
    :precondition (and (holding ?c) (hold-age ?c ?t))
    :effect (and (not (holding ?c)) (not (hold-age ?c ?t)) (sold ?c)))
  (:action pay-1
    :parameters (?c - customer)
    :precondition (and (mode-2) (expired ?c))
    :effect (and (not (expired ?c)) (sold ?c))))
```

Object names: customers c1 to c2; stock levels q0 (empty) to q1; hold ages t0 to t1.

Question: Can every one of the customers end up with a confirmed purchase, i.e. more items sold than were in stock? In the event model this means reaching a state where (and (sold c1) (sold c2)) holds.

Do NOT try to answer the question yourself. Instead, write the PDDL problem file that encodes this
particular design: its objects, its complete initial state, and the goal. A classical planner will then
search it: complete forward search with the FF heuristic decides whether the goal is reachable, and
SATPlan returns the shortest event sequence that reaches it.

Requirements:
- use (:domain inventory) and the object names given above, each declared with its type;
- :init must list every fact that is true initially, including the design facts that describe this
  design and static facts such as counter successors (closed world: anything not listed is false);
- :goal must be (and (sold c1) (sold c2)).

Answer with the problem in one ```pddl block.

completion.text:
Looking at this design and the PDDL domain, I need to identify:
1. The objects and their types
2. The initial state including all true facts
3. The goal

**Analysis:**

The system has:
- 2 customers (c1, c2)
- Stock levels: q0 (empty, 0 items) and q1 (1 item) 
- Ticks: t0 (initial), t1 (one tick later)
- Static counter facts: next-level relationships and tick progression
- Design modes that enable different checkout pathways

The initial state must include:
- All mode-enabling facts (the domain provides four modes)
- Initial stock level (q1 = 1 unit)
- Customers are browsing initially
- Static counter facts (next-level, zero-tick, next-tick, hold-limit)

The question asks whether both customers can end up sold, which exposes the race condition: if both c1 and c2 execute read-1 on the same stock level q1, then both can execute write-stock afterward. Even after c1 decrements stock from q1 to q0, c2's write-stock can still execute (the precondition doesn't verify that the stock level matches what was read), allowing both customers to get holds on the same unit.

```pddl
(define (problem stock-race)
  (:domain inventory)
  (:objects
    c1 c2 - customer
    q0 q1 - level
    t0 t1 - tick
  )
  (:init
    (mode-1)
    (mode-2)
    (mode-3)
    (mode-4)
    (stock q1)
    (browsing c1)
    (browsing c2)
    (next-level q0 q1)
    (zero-tick t0)
    (next-tick t0 t1)
    (hold-limit t1)
  )
  (:goal (and (sold c1) (sold c2)))
)
```
